headline: Match each closer with the most recent unmatched opener
statement: Determine whether a string of (), [], and {} brackets is correctly matched and nested. Every closing bracket must match the latest unmatched opening bracket, and no unmatched bracket may remain.
constraints: Only the six bracket characters occur.
intuition: A nested pair must close before the surrounding pair. Therefore the most recent opener is the only legal match for a closer: exactly the last-in-first-out rule of a stack.
approach: For a closing bracket, reject an empty stack or a mismatched top.
Accept only if the stack is empty at the end.
correctness: The stack contains exactly the unmatched opening brackets of the processed prefix, in their nesting order. A closer must match its top to preserve valid nesting. Rejection detects an impossible match; successful exhaustion with an empty stack proves all brackets were matched correctly.
bruteForce: Repeatedly remove adjacent matching pairs until none remain. This can require O(n²) rescanning; a stack performs each match once.

complexity.explanation: Each bracket is pushed or matched once; all openings may accumulate.

pitfalls: Equal counts do not guarantee correct nesting.
A leading closing bracket is invalid.
Reject leftover openings after the scan.
